questions.q: Which Senegalese island is a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for its history and architecture?
questions.e: Gorée Island is a UNESCO World Heritage Site near Dakar.

questions.q: The Sine-Saloum Delta is important partly because it contains which habitats?
o: Coral reefs in the open ocean
questions.e: The delta includes mangroves, islands and tidal channels.

questions.q: Which river is the main waterway of West Africa and passes through Mali and Niger?
questions.e: The Niger is a major West African river that flows through Mali and Niger.

questions.q: Which mountain range runs across northwestern Africa?
questions.e: The Atlas Mountains extend across Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia.

questions.q: Which West African empire was ruled by Mansa Musa in the 14th century?
questions.e: Mansa Musa ruled the Mali Empire in the 14th century.

questions.q: What is the name of the sea passage between Europe and Africa at Spain and Morocco?
questions.e: The Strait of Gibraltar separates Spain from Morocco.

questions.q: Which African lake is the source region of the White Nile?
questions.e: The White Nile’s source region is associated with Lake Victoria.

questions.q: Which country contains the ancient rock-hewn churches of Lalibela?
questions.e: The churches of Lalibela were carved from rock in Ethiopia.

questions.q: What does biodiversity describe?
o: The variety of living things in an area
The number of roads in a region
The age of a mountain range
questions.e: Biodiversity is the variety of life in a place or across Earth.

questions.q: Which process removes carbon dioxide from the air as plants grow?
questions.e: Plants use carbon dioxide in photosynthesis.

questions.q: Which African ecosystem is characterized by grasslands with scattered trees and seasonal rainfall?
questions.e: Savannas are tropical grasslands with scattered trees and seasonal rainfall.

questions.q: Which country is home to the ancient city of Carthage, near modern Tunis?
questions.e: Ancient Carthage was located in present-day Tunisia.

questions.q: Which desert is found in southern Africa and extends across Botswana and Namibia?
questions.e: The Kalahari covers parts of Botswana, Namibia and South Africa.

questions.q: Which African country is known for the rock-hewn churches of Lalibela and the ancient kingdom of Aksum?
questions.e: Both Lalibela and Aksum are associated with Ethiopia.

questions.q: What is the main role of mangrove roots along tropical coasts?
o: They help stabilize shorelines and provide habitat
questions.e: Mangrove roots help protect coasts and support many species.

questions.q: Which line of latitude passes through northern Africa and crosses the Sahara?
questions.e: The Tropic of Cancer crosses the Sahara in northern Africa.

questions.q: What does “oral history” mainly preserve?
o: Accounts and knowledge passed on by speaking
questions.e: Oral history carries memories and knowledge through spoken accounts.

questions.q: Which language family includes Wolof and Fula?
questions.e: Wolof and Fula are commonly classified within the Niger-Congo language family.

questions.q: Which energy source uses moving air to generate electricity?
questions.e: Wind turbines use moving air to generate electricity.

questions.q: Which geological feature formed as tectonic plates pulled apart in eastern Africa?
questions.e: The Great Rift Valley formed as the crust stretched and separated.

questions.q: Which African country has the city of Timbuktu and the historic Djinguereber Mosque?
questions.e: Timbuktu and the Djinguereber Mosque are in Mali.

questions.q: What is a delta?
o: A mountain peak formed by ice
Land formed where a river deposits sediment near its mouth
A dry valley with no river
questions.e: A delta forms when a river deposits sediment near where it meets another body of water.

questions.q: Which continent contains the Congo Basin rainforest?
questions.e: The Congo Basin rainforest is in Central Africa.

questions.q: Why are protected areas important for migratory animals?
o: They force animals to stay in one place
They can safeguard habitats used at different times of year
questions.e: Protected habitats can support animals as they move between seasonal areas.

questions.q: What long-term practice do the Senegambian stone circles help document?
questions.e: UNESCO links the stone circles and tumuli to funerary practices over a long period.

questions.q: About how many stone circles are included in the four inscribed groups?
questions.e: UNESCO counts 93 circles across the four groups.

questions.q: Which Senegalese complex is the largest among the Senegambian stone-circle sites?
questions.e: UNESCO identifies Sine Ngayène as the largest complex.

questions.q: How many circles does the Sine Ngayène complex contain?
questions.e: UNESCO describes 52 circles at Sine Ngayène.

questions.q: How many circles are in the Wanar complex?
questions.e: UNESCO describes 21 circles at Wanar.

questions.q: What stone material is named in descriptions of the circles’ carved pillars?
questions.e: UNESCO describes the pillars as carved from laterite.

questions.q: What do the associated tumuli mainly represent?
questions.e: UNESCO identifies tumuli as burial mounds.

questions.q: How many standing stones are usually found in one circle?
questions.e: UNESCO gives a range of about eight to fourteen stones per circle.

questions.q: What is the approximate average height of the standing stones?
questions.e: UNESCO describes the stones as averaging around two metres.

questions.q: Which three geo-cultural areas make up Bassari Country?
questions.e: UNESCO identifies these three areas within the property.

questions.q: Between which centuries did Bassari, Fula and Bedik peoples settle in the area, according to UNESCO?
questions.e: UNESCO dates settlement across the area from the 11th to the 19th centuries.

questions.q: What agricultural landscape feature is associated with Bassari Country?
o: Large wheat fields in a desert
questions.e: UNESCO describes terraces and rice paddies in the Bassari landscape.

questions.q: Why is Bassari Country considered a cultural landscape?
o: It reflects long interaction between communities and their environment.
It contains only recently built roads.
It is a single modern city.
It has no connection to local practices.
questions.e: UNESCO explains that land use, social rules and beliefs shaped the landscape.

questions.q: What kind of practices are represented in Bassari Country?
o: Agro-pastoral, social, ritual and spiritual practices
questions.e: UNESCO describes these linked cultural practices.

questions.q: What has the long cultural process of shell-mound building done in the Saloum Delta?
o: Moved the river mouth to Dakar
Helped form stable islets and reclaimed land
questions.e: UNESCO notes shell mounds helped form stable islets over time.

questions.q: What timescale does UNESCO associate with the Saloum shell-mound cultural process?
questions.e: UNESCO describes a cultural process lasting around 2,000 years.

questions.q: Which combination best describes the Saloum Delta’s traditional coastal livelihood?
o: Shellfish gathering, fishing and processing the harvest
questions.e: UNESCO highlights gathering, fishing and preservation of the harvest.

questions.q: What makes parts of the Saloum Delta’s environment ecologically sensitive?
o: Its biodiversity is extensive but fragile.
It is entirely covered by buildings.
It receives no water from rivers or tides.
questions.e: UNESCO describes the delta's biodiversity as extensive and fragile.

questions.q: What physical feature gives Saint-Louis its distinctive island setting?
o: It sits inside a mountain crater.
It is surrounded by the Niger River.
It lies between two arms at the Senegal River mouth.
It stands on an artificial lake.
questions.e: UNESCO describes Saint-Louis between two arms of the river mouth.

questions.q: Which urban features are noted in UNESCO’s description of Saint-Louis?
o: A regular plan, quays and colonial architecture
questions.e: UNESCO cites the town plan, quays and architecture.

questions.q: What role did Saint-Louis play in West Africa before Dakar became the capital?
o: It was an important political, cultural and economic centre.
It was the capital of Ethiopia.
It was a major centre for stone quarrying only.
It was a new city built in the 21st century.
questions.e: UNESCO describes Saint-Louis as an influential regional centre.

questions.q: What do the Stone Circles of Senegambia reveal about the society that built them?
o: It had no knowledge of stone tools.
It was organized enough to sustain skilled construction over centuries.
It used only temporary wooden structures.
questions.e: UNESCO describes a skilled and organized society behind the monuments.

questions.q: Why do UNESCO’s cultural-landscape descriptions consider traditional practices important?
o: They prove that communities never changed.
They show how communities adapted land use to local conditions.
questions.e: The cultural landscape records adaptations to environmental constraints.

questions.q: Which statement about the Stone Circles of Senegambia is accurate?
o: All four groups are on Gorée Island.
The groups are all inside Saint-Louis.
The site is limited to one modern city.
The inscribed groups are located in both Senegal and The Gambia.
questions.e: UNESCO describes a shared, cross-border serial property.

questions.q: Which outside influences are reflected in Lamu Old Town’s architecture?
questions.e: UNESCO describes influences from Arabia, Persia, India and Europe.

questions.q: What street pattern is characteristic of Lamu Old Town?
questions.e: UNESCO describes narrow winding streets.

questions.q: What did the prosperity of Kilwa Kisiwani and Songo Mnara depend on?
questions.e: UNESCO links the ports’ prosperity to Indian Ocean trade.

questions.q: Which mosque is part of the ruins at Kilwa Kisiwani?
questions.e: UNESCO lists the Great Mosque among Kilwa’s ruins.

questions.q: What did Kilwa Kisiwani mint during part of its history?
questions.e: UNESCO says Kilwa minted its own currency.

questions.q: The Meroe archaeological sites are linked to which ancient civilization?
questions.e: UNESCO associates Meroe with Kushite civilization.

questions.q: What kind of tombs are found in Meroe’s burial grounds?
questions.e: UNESCO describes extensive burial grounds of pyramid tombs.

questions.q: Which pair names hinterland centres included with Meroe in the UNESCO property?
questions.e: UNESCO names Musawwarat es-Sufra and Naqa.

questions.q: Which objects from China and Persia were found at Great Zimbabwe?
questions.e: UNESCO reports beads and porcelain from China and Persia.

questions.q: What figure from Great Zimbabwe was adopted as Zimbabwe’s emblem?
questions.e: The Zimbabwe Bird is a soapstone figure and national emblem.

questions.q: Which languages appear together in some Aksumite inscriptions?
questions.e: UNESCO describes inscriptions in Greek, Sabaean and Ge’ez.

questions.q: Which trade route did Aksum control through the port of Adulis?
questions.e: UNESCO notes Aksum’s control of Red Sea trade through Adulis.

questions.q: What does the architecture of Stone Town illustrate about its history?
o: Long-standing exchange between African and Asian shores
The growth of inland cattle routes
questions.e: UNESCO connects its urban form with centuries of seaborne trade.

questions.q: Which plan feature is common in Stone Town houses?
o: A central tower surrounded by moats
Rooms arranged around an open courtyard
questions.e: UNESCO describes houses organized around open courtyards.

questions.q: What kind of doors distinguish many Stone Town houses?
questions.e: UNESCO notes elaborately carved double doors.

questions.q: Which three mosques are named in UNESCO’s description of Timbuktu?
questions.e: These are the three mosques listed for Timbuktu.

questions.q: What role did Timbuktu play in the 15th and 16th centuries?
o: A capital of the Asante kingdom
questions.e: UNESCO describes its intellectual and spiritual role.

questions.q: What was one subject of trade in Timbuktu’s historic markets?
questions.e: UNESCO notes that manuscripts were traded there.

questions.q: How many archaeological sites form part of the Old Towns of Djenné property?
questions.e: UNESCO lists four archaeological sites in the property.

questions.q: Which sites are included in the Djenné archaeological group?
o: Kumasi, Abomey, Kilwa and Songo Mnara
questions.e: UNESCO names these four archaeological sites.

questions.q: What did excavation at Djenné-Djeno reveal about the settlement?
questions.e: UNESCO reports evidence of a pre-Islamic urban structure.

questions.q: Which local construction feature appears in Djenné’s civic buildings?
questions.e: UNESCO describes verticality and buttresses in the architecture.

questions.q: Robben Island’s prison buildings are associated with which historical system?
questions.e: UNESCO links the prison to the Apartheid period.

questions.q: Which other roles did Robben Island serve besides being a prison?
o: A university and a royal court
A trading port and a farm
A hospital and a military base
questions.e: UNESCO lists hospital and military-base uses.

questions.q: What did the buildings of Robben Island bear witness to?
o: Oppression and the later triumph of freedom
The building of the Great Enclosure
questions.e: UNESCO describes this symbolic meaning.

questions.q: When did the maximum-security prison of the Apartheid period begin?
questions.e: UNESCO dates the prison to the 1960s.

questions.q: What was Mapungubwe’s position in southern African trade routes?
o: At the mouth of the Nile
On the Atlantic coast of Senegal
At a crossing of north–south and east–west routes
At the entrance to the Red Sea
questions.e: UNESCO describes its location at these regional route crossings.

questions.q: Which imported objects provide evidence of Mapungubwe’s long-distance trade?
o: Chinese porcelain and Persian glass beads
questions.e: UNESCO records Chinese porcelain and Persian beads.

questions.q: What happened to Mapungubwe’s inhabitants when rainfall declined?
o: They dispersed as farming could no longer support the population
They moved to the coast to build ships
They built a new city in the Sahara
They stopped trading with all neighbours
questions.e: UNESCO links reduced rainfall to the dispersal of inhabitants.

questions.q: Which settlement later became a regional power centre after Mapungubwe declined?
questions.e: UNESCO notes that power shifted north to Great Zimbabwe.

questions.q: What does the Mapungubwe landscape reveal about political organization?
o: A city governed by elected guilds
A network of isolated fishing villages
A kingdom with an elite and sacred leadership
questions.e: UNESCO describes an elite class and sacred kingship.

questions.q: Which natural setting helped support Mapungubwe’s population?
o: A glacier beside the Indian Ocean
A rainforest on the Mediterranean coast
A desert oasis north of the Sahara
Fertile land near the Limpopo–Shashe confluence
questions.e: UNESCO notes the fertility of land near the two rivers.

questions.q: What broad period does UNESCO associate with Mapungubwe’s rise and fall?
questions.e: UNESCO gives this period for the kingdom.

questions.q: Which statement about the old town of Djenné is supported by UNESCO?
o: It was built entirely from coral
It includes an old town and four archaeological sites
It lies on an island in the Indian Ocean
It was founded as a Portuguese fort
questions.e: UNESCO describes this serial property and its four archaeological sites.

questions.q: What does the physical structure of Stone Town reflect?
o: A fusion of Swahili, Indian, Arab and European influences
A Roman and Greek military plan
questions.e: UNESCO describes this fusion of influences.

questions.q: What was the historical role of Stone Town’s location on the Indian Ocean?
o: It protected the city from all contact
It connected the city to the Sahara by camel only
It served as a route to the Arctic
It supported seaborne trade between Africa and Asia
questions.e: UNESCO links the town to extensive seaborne trade.

questions.q: UNESCO dates the major civilization at Great Zimbabwe to which period?
questions.e: UNESCO identifies it as Shona civilization flourishing between the 11th and 15th centuries.

questions.q: Approximately how large is the Great Zimbabwe archaeological site?
questions.e: UNESCO gives the site an area of nearly 80 hectares.

questions.q: What does UNESCO emphasize about Great Zimbabwe’s historical role?
o: It was a Portuguese naval base
It was the first modern capital of Zimbabwe
It was an important medieval trading centre
It was a Roman provincial town
questions.e: UNESCO describes the city as an important trading centre renowned from the Middle Ages.

questions.q: According to UNESCO, Great Zimbabwe is a unique testimony to which civilization?
questions.e: The site bears witness to the Bantu civilization of the Shona.

questions.q: Where are the eleven churches of Lalibela carved?
questions.e: UNESCO describes the churches as monolithic churches carved out of rock.

questions.q: Which ruler is associated with the construction of Lalibela’s churches?
questions.e: UNESCO attributes the building project to King Lalibela.

questions.q: The church of Biete Ghiorgis is connected to the other churches by what?
questions.e: UNESCO notes that trenches connect the isolated Biete Ghiorgis.

questions.q: UNESCO describes Lalibela’s churches as a ‘New Jerusalem’ built after what historical change?
o: Christian pilgrimages to the Holy Land were halted
questions.e: The description links the project to Muslim conquests that halted Christian pilgrimages to the Holy Land.

questions.q: The ancient Aksumite kingdom lasted mainly during which centuries?
questions.e: UNESCO dates the kingdom’s prominence from the 1st to the 8th centuries CE.

questions.q: The ruins at Aksum span approximately which period?
questions.e: UNESCO dates the extensive ruins from the 1st to the 13th century.

questions.q: How tall is the largest standing Aksumite obelisk described by UNESCO?
questions.e: UNESCO says the largest standing obelisk is over 23 metres high.

questions.q: Which three regions lay at the crossroads of the Aksumite kingdom?
o: Europe, East Asia and the Americas
West Africa, South America and Arabia
Africa, Arabia and the Greco-Roman World
questions.e: UNESCO describes Aksum at the crossroads of Africa, Arabia and the Greco-Roman World.

questions.q: What trade commodity from Sudan is specifically mentioned in UNESCO’s account of Aksum?
questions.e: UNESCO notes Aksum’s command of the ivory trade with Sudan.

questions.q: Which two features helped Aksum connect sea and inland trade routes?
o: The ports of Dakar and Saint-Louis
The port of Adulis and routes across north-eastern Africa
The Sahara and the Nile Delta
The Great Lakes and the Congo River
questions.e: UNESCO connects Adulis and inland north-eastern African routes to Aksum’s trade.

questions.q: When was Fort Jesus built?
questions.e: UNESCO dates construction to 1593–1596.

questions.q: What area does the Fort Jesus property cover, including the moat and immediate surroundings?
questions.e: UNESCO gives the property area as 2.36 hectares.

questions.q: Fort Jesus’s layout reflects which design ideal?
o: Renaissance ideals of proportion and geometric harmony
questions.e: UNESCO links its layout to Renaissance proportion and geometric harmony.

questions.q: For how long did the Portuguese keep Fort Jesus under their control?
questions.e: UNESCO says it remained under Portuguese control for one century.

questions.q: Which broad historical significance does UNESCO associate with Fort Jesus?
o: The first railway across East Africa
The end of all trade between Africa and Asia
A Western attempt to control Indian Ocean trade routes
The founding of the Swahili language
questions.e: UNESCO describes it as the first successful Western attempt to rule Indian Ocean trade routes.

questions.q: The Fort Jesus site is located at which edge of Mombasa’s town?
questions.e: UNESCO places it at the southern edge of Mombasa.

questions.q: What did Aksumite emperors continue to do in Aksum after the kingdom’s political decline?
o: They moved the port to Mombasa
questions.e: UNESCO notes that emperors continued to be crowned in Aksum after the 10th-century decline.

questions.q: Which groups does UNESCO name as exchanging cultural values around Fort Jesus?
o: African, Arab, Turkish, Persian and European peoples
questions.e: UNESCO explicitly lists these origins in its account of the fort’s cultural interchange.

questions.q: What distinguishes the churches at Lalibela from a conventional church built with separate blocks?
o: They are made entirely of metal
They are monolithic and carved from the rock
They are underground caves formed by water
questions.e: The churches were carved as monolithic structures from rock.

questions.q: Aksum’s ruins are found near which part of Ethiopia?
questions.e: UNESCO locates ancient Aksum near Ethiopia’s northern border.

questions.q: What is the 1946 law giving citizenship to colonial subjects called?
questions.e: La loi Lamine Guèye de 1946 a accordé la citoyenneté française aux sujets des colonies.

questions.q: Which prime minister did Senghor arrest in 1962?
questions.e: Mamadou Dia, alors Premier ministre, a été arrêté en 1962 après une crise institutionnelle.

questions.q: After 1962, power in Senegal became centred on whom?
questions.e: Après la crise de 1962, le pouvoir s'est concentré davantage autour du président.

questions.q: Who led the PDS party for decades?
questions.e: Abdoulaye Wade a fondé et dirigé le PDS pendant des décennies avant de devenir président en 2000.

questions.q: What role did Macky Sall hold before becoming president?
questions.e: Macky Sall a été Premier ministre sous Abdoulaye Wade avant de rompre avec lui.

questions.q: In which decade did PASTEF rise in Senegalese politics?
questions.e: Le parti PASTEF, dirigé par Ousmane Sonko, a pris de l'importance dans les années 2020.

questions.q: Why did Senegal avoid the coups seen in some neighbours in the 2020s?
questions.e: Le Sénégal est souvent cité pour la stabilité relative de ses transitions démocratiques.

questions.q: What is the National Assembly's main role?
questions.e: L'Assemblée nationale exerce le pouvoir législatif.

questions.q: What does Senegal's Constitutional Council mainly do?
questions.e: Le Conseil constitutionnel valide notamment les résultats électoraux et contrôle la conformité des lois.

questions.q: From which branch is Senegal's judiciary meant to be independent?
questions.e: La Constitution prévoit l'indépendance du pouvoir judiciaire par rapport à l'exécutif.

questions.q: Which level of government did the "Acte 3" reforms aim to strengthen?
questions.e: Les réformes de décentralisation visaient à renforcer les collectivités locales.

questions.q: What is the Plan Sénégal Émergent, launched in 2014?
o: A plan to leave the CFA zone
questions.e: Le Plan Sénégal Émergent est une stratégie de développement économique et social lancée en 2014.

questions.q: Which country's company operates the Sangomar oil field with Senegal?
questions.e: Le champ pétrolier de Sangomar implique notamment l'australien Woodside Energy.

questions.q: What does the Grand Tortue Ahmeyim project produce?
questions.e: Le projet Grand Tortue Ahmeyim concerne un important gisement de gaz offshore.

questions.q: Which institution reviews Senegal's debt and budget?
questions.e: Le FMI suit régulièrement la politique budgétaire et la dette du Sénégal.

questions.q: How many other countries share UEMOA rules with Senegal?
questions.e: L'UEMOA compte huit pays membres partageant la même monnaie et des règles communes.

questions.q: Why was Diamniadio built near Dakar?
questions.e: Diamniadio a été conçue pour désengorger la ville de Dakar.

questions.q: What identity did the Négritude movement celebrate?
questions.e: La Négritude valorisait la fierté de l'identité culturelle noire-africaine.

questions.q: Where was Senghor's partner Aimé Césaire from?
questions.e: Aimé Césaire, poète majeur de la Négritude, venait de la Martinique.

questions.q: What does Sembène's film "Xala" criticize?
questions.e: « Xala » critique la corruption et les élites de l'après-indépendance.

questions.q: Which tragedy did Boubacar Boris Diop write about?
questions.e: Boubacar Boris Diop a notamment écrit sur le génocide rwandais dans « Murambi ».

questions.q: What is Fatou Diome's novel about migration called?
questions.e: « Le Ventre de l'Atlantique » de Fatou Diome traite de la migration.

questions.q: Who argued ancient Egypt was a Black African civilization?
questions.e: Cheikh Anta Diop a défendu l'africanité de la civilisation égyptienne antique.

questions.q: What crop supported the Mouride brotherhood's economy?
questions.e: La confrérie mouride s'est développée autour de la culture communautaire de l'arachide.

questions.q: What does "Khalifa Général" mean?
questions.e: Le Khalife Général dirige une confrérie soufie, comme les mourides ou les tidianes.

questions.q: What relationship does "ndigël" describe?
questions.e: La relation marabout-disciple (ndigël) est centrale dans le soufisme sénégalais.

questions.q: Which country joined Senegal, Mauritania and Mali in the OMVS?
questions.e: La Guinée a rejoint l'OMVS, qui gère le bassin du fleuve Sénégal.

questions.q: In which country is the Manantali Dam located?
questions.e: Le barrage de Manantali se trouve au Mali, mais profite à toute la région.

questions.q: Why was the Diama Dam built?
o: To stop saltwater entering the river
questions.e: Le barrage de Diama empêche la remontée de l'eau salée dans le fleuve.

questions.q: Which coastal area near Saint-Louis faces relocation due to erosion?
questions.e: La Langue de Barbarie, près de Saint-Louis, est particulièrement exposée à l'érosion côtière.

questions.q: Which endangered primate does Senegal try to protect?
questions.e: Le chimpanzé d'Afrique de l'Ouest, menacé, fait l'objet d'efforts de conservation au Sénégal.

questions.q: Between which two areas does Senegal's literacy gap exist?
questions.e: Des écarts importants existent entre zones urbaines et rurales en matière d'alphabétisation.

questions.q: What languages did the "Ubbi Tey Jang Tey" reform promote, besides French?
questions.e: Cette réforme a promu l'usage des langues nationales dans l'enseignement.

questions.q: Besides malaria, which disease has Senegal fought with partners?
questions.e: La tuberculose fait partie des maladies combattues avec des partenaires internationaux.

questions.q: Which 2010s outbreak did Senegal handle well?
questions.e: Le Sénégal a été salué pour sa gestion efficace d'un cas d'Ebola en 2014.

questions.q: Through which organisation does Senegal help mediate regional conflicts?
questions.e: Le Sénégal joue souvent un rôle de médiation via la CEDEAO et l'Union africaine.

questions.q: Which organisation held a summit in Dakar in 1991?
questions.e: Dakar a accueilli un sommet de l'Organisation de la Coopération Islamique en 1991.

questions.q: What did Senegal's "non-alignment" policy mean?
o: Avoiding strict alliance with one power
questions.e: Le non-alignement signifiait éviter une dépendance stricte à un seul bloc de puissance.

questions.q: Where have Senegalese troops served in UN peacekeeping?
o: Conflict zones like the DRC or Mali
questions.e: Le Sénégal envoie régulièrement des troupes dans des missions de l'ONU en Afrique.

questions.q: Which territories did the 1946 Lamine Guèye law cover?
questions.e: La loi Lamine Guèye a étendu la citoyenneté à l'ensemble des territoires d'outre-mer, pas seulement aux Quatre Communes.

questions.q: What did the 1963 constitution strengthen?
questions.e: La Constitution de 1963 a renforcé les pouvoirs présidentiels après la crise de 1962.

questions.q: What ideology shaped Senghor's "Senegalese socialism"?
questions.e: Le « socialisme sénégalais » de Senghor s'inspirait du socialisme démocratique.

questions.q: What kind of reforms marked Abdou Diouf's presidency?
questions.e: Diouf a mis en œuvre des programmes d'ajustement structurel avec le FMI et la Banque mondiale.

questions.q: What did the 2000 election mark for Senegal?
o: Its first peaceful transfer of power
questions.e: 2000 a marqué la première alternance démocratique pacifique au Sénégal.

questions.q: What was the 2016 referendum mainly about?
questions.e: Le référendum de 2016 portait notamment sur la réduction du mandat présidentiel.

questions.q: What controversy came before the 2024 election?
o: A blocked attempt to postpone it
questions.e: Une tentative de report de l'élection a été bloquée par le Conseil constitutionnel en 2024.

questions.q: How was Senegal's 2024 power transfer seen internationally?
questions.e: Cette transition a été saluée comme un exemple de résilience démocratique dans la région.

questions.q: What does Senegal's Economic, Social and Environmental Council advise on?
questions.e: Ce Conseil conseille le gouvernement sur les questions économiques, sociales et environnementales.

questions.q: Which level of government does the High Council of Local Authorities represent?
questions.e: Ce Haut Conseil représente les collectivités locales au niveau national.

questions.q: What does Senegal's Press Code regulate?
questions.e: Le Code de la presse encadre le secteur des médias et du journalisme.

questions.q: Besides agriculture and services, what pillar did the PSE identify?
questions.e: Le PSE identifie l'industrie, l'énergie et les infrastructures comme piliers de transformation.

questions.q: What will Senegal's oil and gas revenue partly fund?
o: Nothing; it's all spent at once
questions.e: Les revenus pétro-gaziers sont en partie destinés à un fonds souverain et à des investissements publics.

questions.q: Which crop is Senegal trying to reduce dependence on?
questions.e: Les politiques agricoles visent à réduire la dépendance exclusive à l'arachide.

questions.q: How large is Senegal's informal economy, roughly?
questions.e: L'économie informelle représente une part très importante de l'activité économique.

questions.q: To which imports does UEMOA's common tariff apply?
o: Goods from outside the UEMOA zone
questions.e: L'UEMOA applique un tarif extérieur commun aux importations venant hors de la zone.

questions.q: What criticism has Négritude faced from later thinkers?
o: Treating "Black" identity as one single thing
questions.e: La Négritude a été critiquée pour une vision parfois essentialiste d'une identité « noire » unique.

questions.q: Which movement does Senghor's "Chants d'ombre" (1945) belong to?
questions.e: « Chants d'ombre » est une œuvre fondatrice de la Négritude.

questions.q: What does Mariama Bâ's "Une si longue lettre" criticize?
questions.e: Le roman critique la polygamie et la condition des femmes.

questions.q: In which language did Boubacar Boris Diop write "Doomi Golo"?
questions.e: « Doomi Golo » a été écrit en wolof par Boubacar Boris Diop.

questions.q: What did Sembène's social-realist films often criticize?
o: Failures of the new independent elites
questions.e: Le cinéma de Sembène critique souvent les élites post-indépendance.

questions.q: What top prize does FESPACO award?
questions.e: L'Étalon de Yennenga est la récompense suprême du FESPACO.

questions.q: What is a "ndigël" in Senegalese Sufi brotherhoods?
questions.e: Le ndigël est une directive donnée par un marabout à ses disciples.

questions.q: Why does Touba have a special administrative status?
o: It is the Mouride brotherhood's centre
questions.e: Touba a un statut particulier lié à son rôle de centre de la confrérie mouride.

questions.q: Why did some disciples settle in Touba in colonial times?
questions.e: Certains disciples s'installaient à Touba pour échapper à des obligations de l'époque coloniale.

questions.q: Between the state and whom have brotherhoods played a go-between role?
questions.e: Les confréries ont souvent joué un rôle d'intermédiaire entre l'État et les populations rurales.

questions.q: What does the OMVS mainly manage?
questions.e: L'OMVS gère l'irrigation, l'hydroélectricité et la navigation sur le fleuve Sénégal.

questions.q: Which countries share Manantali Dam's electricity?
questions.e: L'électricité du barrage de Manantali est partagée entre le Sénégal, le Mali et la Mauritanie.

questions.q: Where does Senegal's Great Green Wall work mostly happen?
questions.e: La contribution sénégalaise à la Grande Muraille Verte concerne surtout la zone sahélienne.

questions.q: What risks threaten communities near Saint-Louis?
questions.e: La montée du niveau de la mer et l'érosion côtière menacent certaines communautés.

questions.q: Whose livelihoods do marine protected areas try to balance with conservation?
questions.e: Les aires marines protégées cherchent à concilier conservation et pêche artisanale.

questions.q: Why are national-language education reforms hard to apply?
questions.e: La diversité des langues nationales complique la production de matériel standardisé.

questions.q: What does Senegal's CMU health reform aim to extend?
questions.e: La CMU vise à étendre la couverture d'assurance maladie à davantage de citoyens.

questions.q: Which body helped Senegal contain its 2014 Ebola case?
questions.e: La coopération rapide avec l'OMS a aidé à contenir le cas d'Ebola de 2014.

questions.q: Besides Dakar and Saint-Louis, where were new universities built?
questions.e: De nouvelles universités ont été créées à Thiès, Ziguinchor, Bambey et ailleurs.

questions.q: Which neighbour has Senegal helped mediate crises in?
questions.e: Le Sénégal a souvent œuvré à la médiation dans des crises politiques en Guinée-Bissau.

questions.q: In what year did Dakar host the first FESMAN festival?
questions.e: Le premier Festival mondial des arts nègres (FESMAN) a eu lieu à Dakar en 1966.

questions.q: Who did the 1966 FESMAN festival bring together?
o: The global Black and African diaspora
questions.e: Le FESMAN a réuni des artistes et intellectuels de la diaspora noire et africaine.

questions.q: Through which organisation does Senegal connect with Lusophone African states?
questions.e: La CEDEAO regroupe des pays francophones, anglophones et lusophones d'Afrique de l'Ouest.

questions.q: What electoral system does Senegal's National Assembly use?
o: A mix of majority and proportional voting
questions.e: Le système électoral sénégalais combine scrutin majoritaire et proportionnel.

questions.q: How is Senegal's press freedom generally rated?
questions.e: Le Sénégal est souvent considéré comme relativement ouvert en matière de liberté de presse, malgré des tensions ponctuelles.

questions.q: How does the Senegalese diaspora mainly help the economy?
questions.e: La diaspora joue un rôle économique important via les transferts de fonds.

questions.q: Why is French still used in Senegalese administration?
questions.e: La politique d'assimilation française explique l'usage persistant du français.

questions.q: Who now sponsors major Senegalese wrestling bouts?
questions.e: Les grands combats de lutte sont aujourd'hui souvent sponsorisés par des entreprises privées.

questions.q: Which organisation's Africa programs helped Senegalese basketball?
questions.e: La NBA a développé des programmes en Afrique qui ont profité au basketball sénégalais.

questions.q: Which 2026 event is Senegal preparing to host?
questions.e: Dakar a été choisie pour accueillir les Jeux Olympiques de la Jeunesse en 2026.

questions.q: Why is Dakar 2026 historic for the Olympics?
o: First Olympic Games held in Africa
questions.e: Les JOJ Dakar 2026 sont les premiers Jeux olympiques organisés en Afrique.

questions.q: Why did Dakar end up hosting these Youth Olympic Games?
o: It took over hosting rights after a delay
questions.e: Dakar a repris l'organisation initialement prévue pour 2022, après un report.

questions.q: What was created to organize the Dakar 2026 Games?
questions.e: Un comité d'organisation national a été créé pour les JOJ Dakar 2026.

questions.q: To what does Senegal's VAT (TVA) generally apply?
questions.e: La TVA s'applique à la majorité des biens et services au Sénégal.

questions.q: Besides France, with which country has trade grown a lot?
questions.e: Les échanges économiques avec la Chine se sont beaucoup développés.

questions.q: What do Senegalese unions mainly negotiate about?
questions.e: Les syndicats négocient surtout sur les salaires et conditions de travail.

questions.q: How long is Senegal's presidential term, since 2016?
questions.e: Le mandat présidentiel est de cinq ans depuis les réformes constitutionnelles.

questions.q: Which body manages judges' careers in Senegal?
o: The Conseil Supérieur de la Magistrature
questions.e: Le Conseil Supérieur de la Magistrature gère la carrière des magistrats.

questions.q: Which regional institution has its headquarters in Dakar?
questions.e: Dakar héberge notamment le siège de la BCEAO et d'autres institutions régionales.

questions.q: What competition threatens Senegal's small-scale fishers?
questions.e: La pêche artisanale fait face à la concurrence de grandes flottes industrielles étrangères.

questions.q: What risk do analysts warn about with Senegal's new oil wealth?
questions.e: Les analystes évoquent le risque de « malédiction des ressources » pour le Sénégal.

questions.q: What does Senegal hope oil revenue will reduce?
o: Imports of fuel and some food
questions.e: Les autorités espèrent réduire la dépendance aux importations de produits raffinés et alimentaires.

questions.q: What had happened to Faye and Sonko shortly before the 2024 election?
questions.e: Faye et Sonko avaient été emprisonnés avant d'être libérés peu avant l'élection de 2024.

questions.q: Which coalition won the 2024 legislative elections?
questions.e: La coalition liée au PASTEF a obtenu la majorité à l'Assemblée nationale en 2024.

questions.q: Despite being French-speaking, what is Senegal culturally rooted in?
questions.e: Le Sénégal reste profondément ancré dans ses langues et traditions africaines malgré le français officiel.
